summary:
A. KPI cards that update live (commit d9dad7f9)
- apps/web/components/analyzer/DashboardKpiStrip.tsx:
  - Live updates. The session series, /v1/streak and the win-rate series now add `#${dbRev}` to their keys, the same way Games in range does, so a games:changed event refreshes every game card. /v1/me/mmr is still unkeyed (it calls SC2Pulse once per Pulse ID), with a comment saying why.
  - "Games today" is renamed "Today's session". It shows "6 games" (the word "games" one size smaller, and "1 game" for one) with a hint of "4W 2L" taken from today's wins and losses. Screen readers hear "4 wins, 2 losses". With no games it shows "0 games" and "No games yet today". The wrong "Keep the streak alive" hint is gone.
  - Card states:
    - A new kpiStatus() helper builds on phase 2a's hasQueryData to sort each card into ready, failed or loading.
    - Loading shows "—" with a skeleton bar where the hint goes. It no longer shows false hints like "No games yet today" while loading.
    - Failed shows "—" plus a "Couldn't load · Retry" button. The button calls that card's own mutate(), sets aria-busy while it runs and ignores repeat presses (the same contract as RequestError's Retry). Its screen-reader name is "Couldn't load your streak. Retry".
    - A real zero still shows "0".
    - Every card follows these states, MMR included. A failed MMR request no longer says "Add a Pulse ID". Games in range keeps its filter label visible while the count loads.
    - RequestError has no compact variant yet, so this is a local button, as the spec allows.
  - Grid: the lead card gets `col-span-2 lg:col-span-1` and the redundant `sm:grid-cols-2` is gone, so phones show rows of 1, 2 and 2. The lead card now has a stable `data-testid="kpi-today-session"`. The old computeGamesToday is replaced by an exported computeTodayRecord().
  - The MMR empty hint is now a Link, "Add a Pulse ID in Settings", to /settings?tab=profile#pulse-id-help.
- apps/web/components/analyzer/WinRateTimeframeMenu.tsx (new): the Win rate label and timeframe menu, moved out of the strip to keep that file short.
  - The trigger has aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls, and ArrowDown or ArrowUp also opens the menu.
  - On open, focus goes to the selected item, or the first one.
  - ArrowUp and ArrowDown wrap, Home and End jump, and Enter or Space picks and returns focus to the trigger.
  - Escape closes the menu and focuses the trigger. Tab closes it and moves on from the trigger's place in the tab order.
  - Menu items and the click-outside catcher are out of the tab order.
  - The menu opens from the label's left edge, because on phones this card is now in the left column.
  - Items are no longer forced to capitals by the card label.
  - The "Own timeframe · ignores the date filter" line from phase 2a is kept.
- apps/web/app/app/loading.tsx and app/app/layout.tsx: the skeleton grids use the same classes (the first card gets col-span-2 lg:col-span-1), so nothing shifts when the cards load.
- apps/web/components/analyzer/settings/SettingsProfile.tsx: the #pulse-id-help panel is collapsed by default, so the MMR link would have had nothing to scroll to. A small effect now opens it when the address hash is #pulse-id-help, and the existing revealSectionAnchor then scrolls to it.

B. Default tab only applies when the session starts on /app (commit 30518e7e)
- apps/web/lib/appSession.ts (new): APP_SESSION_COOKIE ("sc2_app_session") and markAppSession(), which writes `sc2_app_session=1; Path=/; SameSite=Lax` with no Max-Age, inside a try/catch.
- apps/web/components/dashboard/AnalyzerFrame.tsx: calls markAppSession() once on mount (the frame stays mounted across /app routes). The doc comment is updated.
- apps/web/app/app/page.tsx: after the ?opponent and ?tab redirects, defaultTabForThisVisit() runs.
  - If the cookie is present, it returns null without any API call.
  - Otherwise it calls apiFetch('/v1/me/preferences/misc') with AbortSignal.timeout(1500). Any failure, a timeout, "today", an unknown value or no saved value leads to Today.
  - redirect(hrefForTab(...)) runs outside the try block, before render.
- apps/web/components/dashboard/TodayView.tsx: removed the client redirect useEffect, the misc preferences request, the redirected ref and DEFAULT_TAB_APPLIED_KEY. The doc comment is updated. Today no longer makes that request.
- apps/web/components/analyzer/tabs.ts: defaultTabRedirect() also accepts a section slug, so "maps" maps to "battlefield" (the spec's test used pref 'maps').
- apps/web/components/analyzer/settings/SettingsMisc.tsx: the "Today (default)" option was already there (settings-quickwins landed). Only the hint text changed: "Where the dashboard opens the first time you visit it in a browser session. Clicking Today always shows Today."

C. Help (commit 5d9117bf)
- lib/help/articles/analyzer/dashboard-and-analyzer.ts: a new "Today" section covering:
  - the session card shows today's games and W-L and updates as games land;
  - Default tab only applies when you first open the dashboard in a browser session, and clicking Today always shows Today;
  - the MMR card links to the Pulse ID help;
  - per-card Retry.
  It also gets new keywords.
- lib/help/articles/getting-started/settings-overview.ts: the Default tab line in Misc repeats the default-tab rule.
- lib/help/articles/analyzer/analyzer-filters.ts: "Games today" becomes "Today's session".
- I ran `npm run help:index`. The article count is unchanged and the generated index did not change.

changelog_line: Fixed: Today's stat cards now refresh as each game lands. The lead card shows today's games and W-L ("6 games · 4W 2L"), and a card that fails to load says so and offers Retry instead of showing 0. The cards stack cleanly on phones, the Win rate timeframe menu works fully from the keyboard, and the "Default tab" setting only applies when you first open the dashboard in a browser session, so clicking Today always shows Today.
followups:
- help-content-backfill: the spec named a 'today' article that this sibling would write. That article has not landed in my base, so I added a "Today" section to the existing dashboard-and-analyzer article. If the sibling adds a 'today' article, or a "How to read this" header on Today, the integrator should move these four lines into it so they are not duplicated. I did not add a HelpLink on Today, to avoid colliding with that header.
- settings-onboarding-polish-1: I made a 6-line edit to PulseIdEditor in SettingsProfile.tsx (an effect that opens #pulse-id-help when the hash names it). It should merge cleanly next to their Pulse ID changes.
- SettingsMisc.tsx: I changed only the Default tab hint string. The "Today (default)" option was already there from settings-quickwins.
- chrome-nav-polish-1 and shareable-views (W3): the Default tab redirect now lives in app/app/page.tsx (defaultTabForThisVisit) and relies on the sc2_app_session cookie from lib/appSession.ts. A future 'Set as default view' should plug in there, not add a client-side redirect again.
- Known edge, as specified: the cookie is set by AnalyzerFrame, so a session that starts on a non-/app page such as /settings and then clicks Today still gets the default tab once. Setting the cookie in AppShell would close this if wanted.
- Chrome's "continue where you left off" keeps session cookies, so the default tab may apply less often there.
- The Win rate card still shows "0" for a window with no games (existing behaviour; the spec says a real zero shows 0).
- /v1/me/mmr returns empty entries when every SC2Pulse lookup fails, so the card can say "Add a Pulse ID" for a user who already has one. That is an API limitation outside this item.
- The sessions item (W6) can replace the lead card and keep data-testid="kpi-today-session".

summary:
I added two help articles, Replay reviews and Coaching, and linked them from every reviews and coaching page. The help system also gained links to a section inside an article, and a way to keep an article out of search engines. One commit on top of the integration branch (fast-forward worked).

Help system (all paths under apps/web):
- lib/help/types.ts: added the "reviews-coaching" category. Headings can now carry an `id`, which makes a stable section link (/help/<slug>#<id>). A new `noindex` flag keeps an article out of search engines.
- lib/help/categories.ts: added "Reviews & coaching", placed after Builds. It shows up automatically on the /help hub and in Settings > Help.
- lib/help/index.ts: `helpArticlePath(slug, anchor?)` builds section links, and a new `helpArticleAnchors(article)` lists an article's sections.
- lib/help/sitemap.ts leaves noindex articles out; the hub's date comes from the newest article that is listed. app/help/[slug]/page.tsx tells search engines not to index those articles.
- components/help/HelpArticleBody.tsx: on the full article page a section heading gets a real id. In Settings > Help, where many articles share one page, it gets a data attribute instead, so ids can't clash.
- components/help/HelpLink.tsx and LazyHelpLink.tsx: new `anchor` prop. The link points at the section, and the side sheet opens scrolled to that heading with keyboard focus on it.

Articles:
- lib/help/articles/reviews-coaching/replay-reviews.ts: public. Sections: how-it-works, asking-for-a-review, writing-a-review, who-can-review, karma-and-badges, closing-and-sharing, blocking-and-reporting. Every limit, label and number was checked against the API constants, the UI copy and docs/reviews.md.
- lib/help/articles/reviews-coaching/coaching.ts: needs sign-in to follow and is kept out of search engines. Sections: roles-and-linking, locker, practice-sharing, practice-plans, sessions. It says progress is counted from synced replays with fixed rules, and that the workspace never grades or scores play. What the coach can see under practice sharing was checked against the API's consent rules.
- lib/help/articles/index.generated.ts was regenerated with `npm run help:index`.

Links from the pages:
- app/reviews/(board)/page.tsx: "How it works" sits in the header, outside SignedIn, so visitors see it. I removed the hover-only title on "Ask about one of your games" and put a "How to ask" link beside it.

- app/coaching/CoachingWorkspace.tsx: "How coaching works" sits right-aligned in the tab row. Extra beyond the spec: the "Private coaching" screen also links to the article's roles-and-linking section.
- components/reviews/ReviewPage.tsx: the "not enough games" message now reads "Sync at least {n} games with the desktop app to review replays (you have {m}).", followed by "Get the desktop app" (/download) and "Why?" (to who-can-review). The league-required message gets the same "Why?" link. I also fixed its wording, which used to read "verified My league or higher players". ComposerGate is now exported so it can be tested.

changelog_line: Added: Help now explains replay reviews (how to ask, write a review, who can review, karma, closing, blocking) and the coaching workspace, with "How it works" links on the review board, My reviews and Coaching, and a "Why?" link when you can't comment on a review yet.
followups:
- Shared help files: I edited lib/help/types.ts (new category, heading `id`, `noindex`), categories.ts (one entry after Builds), index.ts (`helpArticlePath(slug, anchor?)`, `helpArticleAnchors`), sitemap.ts, app/help/[slug]/page.tsx, HelpArticleBody.tsx, HelpLink.tsx and LazyHelpLink.tsx, plus the regenerated index.generated.ts and the tests articles.test.ts, registry.test.ts and app/__tests__/sitemap.test.ts. help-content-backfill also touches the help registry. When merging, re-run `npm run help:index` and keep both sides of any edits to types.ts and categories.ts.
- The new helpLinkUsage.test.ts fails if any literal HelpLink slug or anchor in the app doesn't resolve. If help-content-backfill adds a similar test, keep one of them.
- Deviations from the spec:
  - The spec gives the category the icon MessageSquareText. The help hub's category cards have no icons, so I left it out rather than make one card different from the rest.
  - The spec names a single reviews-coaching.ts file. I followed the one-file-per-article rule: lib/help/articles/reviews-coaching/replay-reviews.ts and coaching.ts. Later reviews-coaching packs should add their sections to these two files.
  - The spec reads as if `signedInOnly` meant noindex. In the existing help system it only shows a sign-in note, so I added a separate `noindex` flag. Ten existing signed-in-only articles stay indexed as before.
- reviews-coaching-polish-1 also edits components/reviews/ReviewPage.tsx. My changes there are the ComposerGate function at the end of the file plus one import each from LazyHelpLink and lib/reviews.
- The signed-out "How the Review Exchange works" strip (ReviewExchangeIntro) has no "Learn more" link to point at /help/replay-reviews. I didn't add one, because the header's "How it works" link sits directly above it.
- Not handled: the replay-reviews article is public and indexed even when NEXT_PUBLIC_REVIEWS_ENABLED is off or set to admins. In that case its /reviews links lead to a 404. If production isn't on "on", the article needs to follow the rollout flag.
